name: LIBERO
summary: LIBERO provides 130 language-conditioned manipulation tasks organized into suites that isolate different distribution shifts — spatial, object, goal and long-horizon. Designed for lifelong and transfer learning research, it was adopted almost universally as the standard simulated evaluation for VLA fine-tuning, which at least makes results across papers roughly comparable.
innovation: Task suites deliberately factored by type of generalization rather than lumped into one average.
Procedural task and scene generation supporting controlled distribution shift.
matters: The most cited comparison point in VLA papers, for better and for worse.
limits: Simulation only, with a well-documented gap to real-robot performance.
Increasingly saturated — top methods cluster tightly enough that the ranking is mostly noise.
lineage: Descends from robomimic's benchmarking tradition, adapted to language-conditioned multitask evaluation.
